column7: 2026-11-05: parseBytes: SI units (kB/MB/GB…) deliberately unsupported (throw SyntaxError 'Unsupported unit') until user hears from storage team on how to read them (1000 vs 1024). My choices: negative/signed input, exponents and '.5'/'5.' rejected; space optional; result unrounded.

2026-11-05: Storage team decision (relayed by user): on this branch parseBytes must read the non-i units as powers of 1024, since users paste sizes from Windows Explorer: '1 KB' and '1 kB' are 1024, '1 MB' is 1048576, and so on. Not implemented yet; user said to add them next time. Until then they throw SyntaxError 'Unsupported unit'.

2026-11-05: billing-svc: parseBytes already exists (inherited commit 1d59f5d, same as storage-app): plain numbers + B + KiB..YiB, SI units (kB/MB/GB) throw SyntaxError 'Unsupported unit'. User wants no SI units yet on this branch. The storage-app 'non-i units = 1024' decision is that branch's only; do not apply it here. Tests/types already present; npm test passes (54).

2026-11-05: billing-svc: when SI units (kB/MB/GB...) are added on this branch, read them as strict SI powers of 1000 ('1 MB' = 1,000,000 bytes), matching prettyBytes' default output. Reason: billing quotes in strict SI. Overrides/contrasts storage-app's 1024 reading, which is that branch only. Not implemented yet; still throws 'Unsupported unit'.

2026-11-05: parseBytes now implemented (per storage team): kB, KB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB, YB are all powers of 1024. Other casings (kb, Kb, mb, yb) still throw 'Unsupported unit' - my choice, keeps units case-sensitive. Documented in readme and index.d.ts.
